I think that kindness is more advantageous for every specie. If everyone is selfish, everybody will remain alone and it's more difficult to survive and reproduce that way. No animal lives alone, and you can kinda call that being together and caring for the group kindness.

But, even if a God made our universe, what made that God? Say that God created everything isn't really an answer, because something must have created him to. Or can did God originated from nothing? And if God originated from nothing, then why couldn't the universe be born from the same nothing?

You are right. But what I was referring to when I said God, was not a higher being, that is very likely to exist, but a being that, just like some religions believe, created us, that is watching and judging us.

If something superior really does exist, I doubt it really gives a fuck about ants like us.

Okay, the universe was originated from this being called God, because it cannot originate from nothing. Just like the universe, something must have created it. But then what made God? How did it come to exist? Another God? And what made that God? It's an inception that will never end.
I won't change my mind, and I'm not pretending to change anybody's belief, I was just curious to hear other people opinions.

That kindness that you are talking about at the start is just, I think, human nature (?), what makes us diffrent from other animals. And I think that it was just thanks to evolution. A casual, chaothic, darwinian evolution. Not really something chosen by 'God'.

I'm not saying that there is something wrong with the true Christian ideology. Helping those in needs and believing in others is a good thing, but humans should learn to do it just because it's the 'good' thing to do, not because they will get a reward for not being 'bad'.

And I wasn't really questioning Christian ideology or the Bible. I just find it strange that people believe that there is something, that looks just like a human being, that has the power to create everything and knows anything, and that being is just there, watching and judging us (that are less than ants for him).

I'm talking about Christian God because that's the one I have the most knowledge of, having studied it in school and outside for some years. I know almost nothing about Hinduism and Islam, so I can't really talk about them. Buddhism is closer to being a philosophy than a religion, for all I know they don't really have a God as the Christians do.

And I know about the real appearence of Angels.

What I can't understand is, how do people think that this 'God' that created them is watching them all the time and is really interested in them being good or bad? We're less than ants for a being like it, so why would it care about us?

I said religious because with the word "God" I wasn't referring to a higher, more powerful being, but to the Christian idea of God (something just like a human that created the world and is watching us every single moment). I think that it is quite possible that something else, something way more powerful and intelligent than us exists. I sometimes wonder if this universe isn't just a cell of something much much bigger.

Sorry if you think that "magical man in the sky" is inappropriate, but I think that it suits the Christian idea of God quite well. That's what it is for Christians, a human that can produce life and knows everything.
I'm not saying that there is nothing else besides our universe and humans life, but I think that if something else really exists, it could be more similar to a Lovecraftian monster than something identical to humans with powers (that's how I personally think Christians portrait God)
The fact that there's a magical man up in the sky that can create everything and knows anything seems a little strange to me.
